issues.description: The problem statement specifies a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) for SealSaloon (UML and textual description). The solution implementation instead provides a static method named receiveDelivery(String, int, int). The template's Main (commented example) also calls acceptSupplyDelivery. This name mismatch between the specification, the example usage in the template, and the solution creates confusion about the required API and may lead students to implement the method with the wrong name or to be unsure which name the tests expect.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the API consistent across all artifacts. Rename the solution method receiveDelivery to acceptSupplyDelivery (keeping it static and with parameters (String, int, int)), and/or update the problem statement and template example to refer to receiveDelivery. Ensure the example Main invocation matches the final chosen method name and that the method signature matches the specification.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML and textual requirements) refers to a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) to register ingredient deliveries into the shared stock, but the solution implementation defines this operation as receiveDelivery(String, int, int). This difference in method name for the same conceptual operation (accepting a supply delivery) creates a mapping confusion for students who will look for acceptSupplyDelivery in the provided code or tests but find receiveDelivery instead.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution method receiveDelivery to acceptSupplyDelivery (keeping it static and with the same parameters and behavior), or alternatively update the problem statement / UML to reference receiveDelivery so the method name is consistent across artifacts.
